request.current_synthesis: Observed evidence: M1 passed all controlled implementation checks: zero-command equilibrium was exact, a bounded command changed state, repeated transitions matched to 0, and resets correctly reached extended, open, and folded configurations. M2 measured the compiled model as 2 ms explicit Euler with Newton solver, two joints each with 0.5 N m s damping and 0.01 kg m^2 armature, and two 5 N m nominal motor limits. Across representative extended, open, and folded postures, saturated 160 ms pulses reached about 10 rad/s joint speed and paired commands about 14.1-14.2 rad/s; single-joint cross-joint speeds were roughly 0.09-0.16 rad/s. A 20 ms half-command pulse displaced the endpoint 2.63-3.20 cm and met the measurement settling criterion after about 0.126-0.132 s. A 0.8 s zero-command free-decay trial reduced the imposed 1.166 rad/s joint-speed norm to below 1e-14 of its initial value in all three postures. Interpretation: the compiled system has substantial actuation and strong passive decay, so the physical plant is not presently shown to be authority-limited or intrinsically unable to stabilize; however, the large transient speeds and 20 ms action holding can still make policy braking and entry timing decisive. The controlled traces do not distinguish reach from hold failures because no learned policy was run, do not cover the official radius-angle panel, do not record contacts or continuous tolerance excursions, and use representative rather than IK-swept postures. Competing explanations remain: (1) a baseline policy can reach and hold once trained on the relevant geometry, making exposure/generalization the main gap; (2) the baseline reaches but overshoots or interrupts the sampled hold, making terminal velocity-aware regulation the main gap; or (3) branch/inner-radius geometry creates selective failures despite adequate local dynamics.
